title: When should an AI-driven RPG ask the player to clarify an action?
author: melty_program
selftext:
I am working on a text-driven RPG where players type what they say or try to do. One design problem I keep coming back to is when the game should ask a question instead of interpreting the line and moving on.



For example:



"Maybe we should open the chest." — a suggestion to the party, or an attempt to open it?



"Fine, take it." — agreement, sarcasm, or something said to a different character?



Asking every time would make conversation tedious. Guessing wrong could spend an item or commit the whole party to something they did not intend. My preference is to clarify before an irreversible change, while letting ordinary dialogue continue.



For anyone building this kind of game: what does the clarification look like in your UI? An NPC asking a short question, a restatement of the intended action, or something else? I would especially like to hear about a case where the extra question helped, or made the interaction worse.
